audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Deuteronomy / Devarim wilderness-border and Sihon narrative retelling, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Seir/Edom, Moab, and Ammon boundaries; wilderness provision; Rephaim traditions; Sihon diplomacy, hardening, conquest, and total-destruction language.

verses.restored: We turned and set out toward wilderness by way of Sea of Reeds, as YHWH spoke to me, and circled Mount Seir many days.

familiar.text: Then we turned, and took our journey into the wilderness by the way of the Red sea, as the LORD spake unto me: and we compassed mount Seir many days.

modern.text: Then we turned back and headed for the wilderness by way of the Red Sea, as the LORD had instructed me, and for many days we wandered around Mount Seir.

verses.restored: YHWH spoke to me, saying,

familiar.text: And the LORD spake unto me, saying,

modern.text: At this time the LORD said to me,

verses.restored: Long enough you have circled this mountain; turn yourselves northward.

familiar.text: Ye have compassed this mountain long enough: turn you northward.

modern.text: “You have been wandering around this hill country long enough; turn to the north

original.text: רַב לָכֶ֕ם סֹ֖ב אֶת הָהָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה פְּנ֥וּ לָכֶ֖ם צָפֹֽנָה

verses.restored: Command the people, saying: You are passing through border of your brothers, sons of Esau dwelling in Seir, and they will fear you. Guard yourselves greatly.

familiar.text: And command thou the people, saying, Ye are to pass through the coast of your brethren the children of Esau, which dwell in Seir; and they shall be afraid of you: take ye good heed unto yourselves therefore:

modern.text: and command the people: ‘You will pass through the territory of your brothers, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir. They will be afraid of you, so you must be very careful.

original.text: וְאֶת הָעָם֮ צַ֣ו לֵאמֹר֒ אַתֶּ֣ם עֹֽבְרִ֗ים בִּגְבוּל֙ אֲחֵיכֶ֣ם בְּנֵי עֵשָׂ֔ו הַיֹּשְׁבִ֖ים בְּשֵׂעִ֑יר וְיִֽירְא֣וּ מִכֶּ֔ם וְנִשְׁמַרְתֶּ֖ם מְאֹֽד

verses.restored: Do not contend with them, for I will not give you from their land even tread of foot, because Mount Seir I gave to Esau as possession.

familiar.text: Meddle not with them; for I will not give you of their land, no, not so much as a foot breadth; because I have given mount Seir unto Esau for a possession.

modern.text: Do not provoke them, for I will not give you any of their land, not even a footprint, because I have given Mount Seir to Esau as his possession.

original.text: אַל תִּתְגָּר֣וּ בָ֔ם כִּ֠י לֹֽא אֶתֵּ֤ן לָכֶם֙ מֵֽאַרְצָ֔ם עַ֖ד מִדְרַ֣ךְ כַּף רָ֑גֶל כִּֽי יְרֻשָּׁ֣ה לְעֵשָׂ֔ו נָתַ֖תִּי אֶת הַ֥ר שֵׂעִֽיר

verses.restored: Food you shall buy from them with silver and eat, and water you shall buy from them with silver and drink.

familiar.text: Ye shall buy meat of them for money, that ye may eat; and ye shall also buy water of them for money, that ye may drink.

modern.text: You are to pay them in silver for the food you eat and the water you drink.’”

original.text: אֹ֣כֶל תִּשְׁבְּר֧וּ מֵֽאִתָּ֛ם בַּכֶּ֖סֶף וַאֲכַלְתֶּ֑ם וְגַם מַ֜יִם תִּכְר֧וּ מֵאִתָּ֛ם בַּכֶּ֖סֶף וּשְׁתִיתֶֽם

verses.restored: For YHWH your Divine has blessed you in all work of your hand; he knows your walking through this great wilderness. These forty years YHWH your Divine has been with you; you have lacked nothing.

familiar.text: For the LORD thy God hath blessed thee in all the works of thy hand: he knoweth thy walking through this great wilderness: these forty years the LORD thy God hath been with thee; thou hast lacked nothing.

modern.text: Indeed, the LORD your God has blessed you in all the work of your hands. He has watched over your journey through this vast wilderness. The LORD your God has been with you these forty years, and you have lacked nothing.

original.text: כִּי֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ בֵּֽרַכְךָ֗ בְּכֹל֙ מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יָדֶ֔ךָ יָדַ֣ע לֶכְתְּךָ֔ אֶת הַמִּדְבָּ֥ר הַגָּדֹ֖ל הַזֶּ֑ה זֶ֣ה אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֗ה יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ עִמָּ֔ךְ לֹ֥א חָסַ֖רְתָּ דָּבָֽר

verses.restored: We passed by our brothers, sons of Esau dwelling in Seir, away from Arabah road, from Elath and Ezion-geber, and turned and passed by way of wilderness of Moab.

familiar.text: And when we passed by from our brethren the children of Esau, which dwelt in Seir, through the way of the plain from Elath, and from Eziongaber, we turned and passed by the way of the wilderness of Moab.

modern.text: So we passed by our brothers, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir. We turned away from the Arabah road, which comes up from Elath and Ezion-geber, and traveled along the road of the Wilderness of Moab.

original.text: וַֽנַּעֲבֹ֞ר מֵאֵ֧ת אַחֵ֣ינוּ בְנֵי עֵשָׂ֗ו הַיֹּֽשְׁבִים֙ בְּשֵׂעִ֔יר מִדֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ הָֽעֲרָבָ֔ה מֵאֵילַ֖ת וּמֵעֶצְיֹ֣ן גָּ֑בֶר וַנֵּ֨פֶן֙ וַֽנַּעֲבֹ֔ר דֶּ֖רֶךְ מִדְבַּ֥ר מוֹאָֽב

verses.restored: YHWH said to me, Do not harass Moab and do not contend with them in battle, for I will not give you from their land as possession; for to sons of Lot I gave Ar as possession.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto me, Distress not the Moabites, neither contend with them in battle: for I will not give thee of their land for a possession; because I have given Ar unto the children of Lot for a possession.

modern.text: Then the LORD said to me, “Do not harass the Moabites or provoke them to war, for I will not give you any of their land, because I have given Ar to the descendants of Lot as their possession.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י אֶל תָּ֨צַר֙ אֶת מוֹאָ֔ב וְאַל תִּתְגָּ֥ר בָּ֖ם מִלְחָמָ֑ה כִּ֠י לֹֽא אֶתֵּ֨ן לְךָ֤ מֵֽאַרְצוֹ֙ יְרֻשָּׁ֔ה כִּ֣י לִבְנֵי ל֔וֹט נָתַ֥תִּי אֶת עָ֖ר יְרֻשָּֽׁה

modern.text: (The Emites used to live there, a people great and many, as tall as the Anakites.

verses.restored: Rephaim they also were reckoned, like Anakim, but Moabites call them Emim.

familiar.text: Which also were accounted giants, as the Anakims; but the Moabites call them Emims.

modern.text: Like the Anakites, they were also regarded as Rephaim, though the Moabites called them Emites.

original.text: רְפָאִ֛ים יֵחָשְׁב֥וּ אַף הֵ֖ם כָּעֲנָקִ֑ים וְהַמֹּ֣אָבִ֔ים יִקְרְא֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם אֵמִֽים

modern.text: The Horites used to live in Seir, but the descendants of Esau drove them out. They destroyed the Horites from before them and settled in their place, just as Israel did in the land that the LORD gave them as their possession.)

original.text: וּבְשֵׂעִ֞יר יָשְׁב֣וּ הַחֹרִים֮ לְפָנִים֒ וּבְנֵ֧י עֵשָׂ֣ו יִֽירָשׁ֗וּם וַיַּשְׁמִידוּם֙ מִפְּנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיֵּשְׁב֖וּ תַּחְתָּ֑ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֧ר עָשָׂ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לְאֶ֨רֶץ֙ יְרֻשָּׁת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁר נָתַ֥ן יְהוָ֖ה לָהֶֽם

familiar.text: Now rise up, said I, and get you over the brook Zered. And we went over the brook Zered.

modern.text: “Now arise and cross over the Brook of Zered.” So we crossed over the Brook of Zered.

familiar.text: And the space in which we came from Kadeshbarnea, until we were come over the brook Zered, was thirty and eight years; until all the generation of the men of war were wasted out from among the host, as the LORD sware unto them.

modern.text: The time we spent traveling from Kadesh-barnea until we crossed over the Brook of Zered was thirty-eight years, until that entire generation of fighting men had perished from the camp, as the LORD had sworn to them.

modern.text: Indeed, the LORD’s hand was against them, to eliminate them from the camp, until they had all perished.

modern.text: (That too was regarded as the land of the Rephaim, who used to live there, though the Ammonites called them Zamzummites.

modern.text: They were a people great and many, as tall as the Anakites. But the LORD destroyed them from before the Ammonites, who drove them out and settled in their place,

modern.text: just as He had done for the descendants of Esau who lived in Seir, when He destroyed the Horites from before them. They drove them out and have lived in their place to this day.

familiar.text: And the Avims which dwelt in Hazerim, even unto Azzah, the Caphtorims, which came forth out of Caphtor, destroyed them, and dwelt in their stead.)

modern.text: And the Avvim, who lived in villages as far as Gaza, were destroyed by the Caphtorites, who came out of Caphtor and settled in their place.) The Defeat of Sihon (Numbers 21:21–30)

original.text: וְהָֽעַוִּ֛ים הַיֹּשְׁבִ֥ים בַּחֲצֵרִ֖ים עַד עַזָּ֑ה כַּפְתֹּרִים֙ הַיֹּצְאִ֣ים מִכַּפְתּ֔וֹר הִשְׁמִידֻ֖ם וַיֵּשְׁב֥וּ תַחְתָּֽם

familiar.text: Rise ye up, take your journey, and pass over the river Arnon: behold, I have given into thine hand Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land: begin to possess it, and contend with him in battle.

modern.text: “Arise, set out, and cross the Arnon Valley. See, I have delivered into your hand Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land. Begin to take possession of it and engage him in battle.

familiar.text: This day will I begin to put the dread of thee and the fear of thee upon the nations that are under the whole heaven, who shall hear report of thee, and shall tremble, and be in anguish because of thee.

modern.text: This very day I will begin to put the dread and fear of you upon all the nations under heaven. They will hear the reports of you and tremble in anguish because of you.”

familiar.text: And I sent messengers out of the wilderness of Kedemoth unto Sihon king of Heshbon with words of peace, saying,

modern.text: So from the Wilderness of Kedemoth I sent messengers with an offer of peace to Sihon king of Heshbon, saying,

original.text: וָאֶשְׁלַ֤ח מַלְאָכִים֙ מִמִּדְבַּ֣ר קְדֵמ֔וֹת אֶל סִיח֖וֹן מֶ֣לֶךְ חֶשְׁבּ֑וֹן דִּבְרֵ֥י שָׁל֖וֹם לֵאמֹֽר

verses.restored: Let me pass through your land; by road, by road I will go, I will not turn right or left.

familiar.text: Let me pass through thy land: I will go along by the high way, I will neither turn unto the right hand nor to the left.

modern.text: “Let us pass through your land; we will stay on the main road. We will not turn to the right or to the left.

original.text: אֶעְבְּרָ֣ה בְאַרְצֶ֔ךָ בַּדֶּ֥רֶךְ בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֵלֵ֑ךְ לֹ֥א אָס֖וּר יָמִ֥ין וּשְׂמֹֽאול

verses.restored: Food for silver you shall sell me and I will eat, and water for silver you shall give me and I will drink; only let me pass on foot,

familiar.text: Thou shalt sell me meat for money, that I may eat; and give me water for money, that I may drink: only I will pass through on my feet;

modern.text: You can sell us food to eat and water to drink in exchange for silver. Only let us pass through on foot,

original.text: אֹ֣כֶל בַּכֶּ֤סֶף תַּשְׁבִּרֵ֨נִי֙ וְאָכַ֔לְתִּי וּמַ֛יִם בַּכֶּ֥סֶף תִּתֶּן לִ֖י וְשָׁתִ֑יתִי רַ֖ק אֶעְבְּרָ֥ה בְרַגְלָֽי

verses.restored: as sons of Esau dwelling in Seir and Moabites dwelling in Ar did for me, until I cross Jordan into land YHWH our Divine is giving us.

familiar.text: (As the children of Esau which dwell in Seir, and the Moabites which dwell in Ar, did unto me;) until I shall pass over Jordan into the land which the LORD our God giveth us.

modern.text: just as the descendants of Esau who live in Seir and the Moabites who live in Ar did for us, until we cross the Jordan into the land that the LORD our God is giving us.”

original.text: כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר עָֽשׂוּ לִ֜י בְּנֵ֣י עֵשָׂ֗ו הַיֹּֽשְׁבִים֙ בְּשֵׂעִ֔יר וְהַמּ֣וֹאָבִ֔ים הַיֹּשְׁבִ֖ים בְּעָ֑ר עַ֤ד אֲשֶֽׁר אֶֽעֱבֹר֙ אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן אֶל הָאָ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁר יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ נֹתֵ֥ן לָֽנוּ

verses.restored: But Sihon king of Heshbon was unwilling to let us pass through him, for YHWH your Divine hardened his spirit and made his heart stubborn, in order to give him into your hand, as this day.

familiar.text: But Sihon king of Heshbon would not let us pass by him: for the LORD thy God hardened his spirit, and made his heart obstinate, that he might deliver him into thy hand, as appeareth this day.

modern.text: But Sihon king of Heshbon would not let us pass through, for the LORD your God had made his spirit stubborn and his heart obstinate, that He might deliver him into your hand, as is the case this day.

original.text: וְלֹ֣א אָבָ֗ה סִיחֹן֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ חֶשְׁבּ֔וֹן הַעֲבִרֵ֖נוּ בּ֑וֹ כִּֽי הִקְשָׁה֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ אֶת רוּח֗וֹ וְאִמֵּץ֙ אֶת לְבָב֔וֹ לְמַ֛עַן תִּתּ֥וֹ בְיָדְךָ֖ כַּיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: YHWH said to me, See, I have begun to give Sihon and his land before you. Begin, possess, to possess his land.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto me, Behold, I have begun to give Sihon and his land before thee: begin to possess, that thou mayest inherit his land.

modern.text: Then the LORD said to me, “See, I have begun to deliver Sihon and his land over to you. Now begin to conquer and possess his land.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י רְאֵ֗ה הַֽחִלֹּ֨תִי֙ תֵּ֣ת לְפָנֶ֔יךָ אֶת סִיחֹ֖ן וְאֶת אַרְצ֑וֹ הָחֵ֣ל רָ֔שׁ לָרֶ֖שֶׁת אֶת אַרְצֽוֹ

verses.restored: Sihon came out to meet us, he and all his people, for battle at Jahaz.

familiar.text: Then Sihon came out against us, he and all his people, to fight at Jahaz.

modern.text: So Sihon and his whole army came out for battle against us at Jahaz.

original.text: וַיֵּצֵא֩ סִיחֹ֨ן לִקְרָאתֵ֜נוּ ה֧וּא וְכָל עַמּ֛וֹ לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה יָֽהְצָה

verses.restored: YHWH our Divine gave him before us, and we struck him and his sons and all his people.

familiar.text: And the LORD our God delivered him before us; and we smote him, and his sons, and all his people.

modern.text: And the LORD our God delivered him over to us, and we defeated him and his sons and his whole army.

original.text: וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֛הוּ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ לְפָנֵ֑ינוּ וַנַּ֥ךְ אֹת֛וֹ וְאֶת בנו וְאֶת כָּל עַמּֽוֹ

verses.restored: We captured all his cities at that time and devoted to destruction every city—men, women, and little ones; we left no survivor.

familiar.text: And we took all his cities at that time, and utterly destroyed the men, and the women, and the little ones, of every city, we left none to remain:

modern.text: At that time we captured all his cities and devoted to destruction the people of every city, including women and children. We left no survivors.

original.text: וַנִּלְכֹּ֤ד אֶת כָּל עָרָיו֙ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔וא וַֽנַּחֲרֵם֙ אֶת כָּל עִ֣יר מְתִ֔ם וְהַנָּשִׁ֖ים וְהַטָּ֑ף לֹ֥א הִשְׁאַ֖רְנוּ שָׂרִֽיד

verses.restored: Only livestock we plundered for ourselves, and spoil of cities we captured.

familiar.text: Only the cattle we took for a prey unto ourselves, and the spoil of the cities which we took.

modern.text: We carried off for ourselves only the livestock and the plunder from the cities we captured.

original.text: רַ֥ק הַבְּהֵמָ֖ה בָּזַ֣זְנוּ לָ֑נוּ וּשְׁלַ֥ל הֶעָרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לָכָֽדְנוּ

verses.restored: From Aroer on edge of wadi Arnon and city in wadi, even to Gilead, there was no city too high for us; YHWH our Divine gave all before us.

familiar.text: From Aroer, which is by the brink of the river of Arnon, and from the city that is by the river, even unto Gilead, there was not one city too strong for us: the LORD our God delivered all unto us:

modern.text: From Aroer on the rim of the Arnon Valley, along with the city in the valley, even as far as Gilead, not one city had walls too high for us. The LORD our God gave us all of them.

original.text: מֵֽעֲרֹעֵ֡ר אֲשֶׁר֩ עַל שְׂפַת נַ֨חַל אַרְנֹ֜ן וְהָעִ֨יר אֲשֶׁ֤ר בַּנַּ֨חַל֙ וְעַד הַגִּלְעָ֔ד לֹ֤א הָֽיְתָה֙ קִרְיָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׂגְבָ֖ה מִמֶּ֑נּוּ אֶת הַכֹּ֕ל נָתַ֛ן יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ לְפָנֵֽינוּ

verses.restored: Only to land of sons of Ammon you did not draw near, all side of wadi Jabbok and cities of hill country, and wherever YHWH our Divine commanded us.

familiar.text: Only unto the land of the children of Ammon thou camest not, nor unto any place of the river Jabbok, nor unto the cities in the mountains, nor unto whatsoever the LORD our God forbad us.

modern.text: But you did not go near the land of the Ammonites, or the land along the banks of the Jabbok River, or the cities of the hill country, or any place that the LORD our God had forbidden.

original.text: רַ֛ק אֶל אֶ֥רֶץ בְּנֵי עַמּ֖וֹן לֹ֣א קָרָ֑בְתָּ כָּל יַ֞ד נַ֤חַל יַבֹּק֙ וְעָרֵ֣י הָהָ֔ר וְכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר צִוָּ֖ה יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ

translation_notes: Edom, Moab, and Ammon are given protected territorial boundaries. Israel is told not to seize their land and to purchase food and water.
The chapter preserves layered memories of earlier peoples and dispossessions; these are ancient ethnographic traditions, not moral endorsements of conquest.
The peaceful transit request to Sihon is part of Moses' retelling, while hardening language shifts responsibility toward Divine purpose; this tension requires theological audit.
Verse 34 explicitly includes men, women, and children in total-destruction warfare. It must not be softened or defended as modern ethics.
Protected borders around kin peoples sit in unresolved tension with destruction of Sihon's population.
safety_note: Never use Deuteronomy 2 to justify genocide, child killing, colonial conquest, terrorizing populations, or claims that Divine hardening removes human responsibility. Preserve its protected-border ethic while rejecting the total-destruction campaign as a model for any modern people.
